title: Google Signs Superhot Geothermal Power Pact, Kazakhstan Awards 2.5 Bcm Gas Plant to China, and Equinor Fights Cyberattack Amid Tight Gas Markets
subhead: Google strikes a world-first superhot geothermal deal with Quaise Energy as Kazakhstan signs a 2.5 bcm Kashagan gas plant deal with a Chinese consortium, Equinor battles a live cyberattack during elevated gas prices, and US Senate lawmakers advance permitting reform.

sections.heading: Google Signs World-First Superhot Geothermal Deal With Quaise Energy
sections.body:
Google signed a landmark agreement this week with startup Quaise Energy to procure electricity generated from superhot rock formations at Oregon's Newberry Volcano, OilPrice reports, marking the world's first commercial deal for millimeter-wave deep geothermal power. The pact targets round-the-clock, zero-carbon baseload electricity to feed hyperscale AI data centers that cannot rely solely on intermittent wind and solar output.

In US energy policy, The Hill reports the Senate cleared another series of procedural votes on Wednesday to advance the bipartisan permitting reform bill (BAAJA) aimed at accelerating grid transmission and energy project approvals. Together, corporate baseload deals and federal permitting momentum point to rising urgency around power availability for industrial and AI load growth.
sections.whyItMatters: Superhot geothermal power promises firm, 24/7 clean electricity independent of weather or long-distance transmission queues, offering hyperscalers a scalable alternative to natural gas peakers and delayed nuclear builds.

sections.heading: Kazakhstan Awards 2.5 Bcm Kashagan Gas Plant Contract to China
sections.body:
Kazakhstan's state gas company QazaqGaz signed a turnkey contract with a Chinese consortium to build a 2.5 billion cubic meter (bcm) annual gas processing plant fed by the giant Kashagan oilfield, OilPrice reports. Under the turnkey arrangement, Chinese engineering firms will manage every phase of the facility, expanding Beijing's industrial footprint across Central Asia's upstream hydrocarbon infrastructure.

At the same time, Bloomberg reports China's crude oil imports rebounded as Beijing resumed strategic stockpiling, even as OilPrice notes that high global fossil-fuel costs from the Iran war are pushing China to burn less oil and coal overall while accelerating domestic renewable additions to shrink its import bill.
sections.whyItMatters: Locking in Kashagan's gas-processing infrastructure reinforces China's long-term overland energy access in Central Asia while helping Beijing hedge against maritime disruption in the Middle East.

sections.heading: Equinor Battles Cyberattack While Gas Prices Stay Elevated
sections.body:
Norwegian energy major Equinor—Europe's single largest pipeline gas supplier—is fighting an ongoing cyberattack on its IT systems at a moment when the Strait of Hormuz crisis has kept European natural gas prices nearly triple last year's levels, OilPrice reports. The intrusion follows an FBI warning last week that state-aligned hackers and criminal syndicates are using an AI-powered tool to breach corporate networks.

In the UK water and utility sector, OilPrice cites Financial Times reporting that the latest US bidder for distressed utility Thames Water offered to raise its bid by £1 billion on condition that regulators waive pollution mitigation requirements until 2030, sparking backlash over environmental compliance standards.
sections.whyItMatters: An active cyberattack against Europe's top pipeline gas supplier exposes operational vulnerability across energy networks precisely when winter storage buffers are thin and LNG flows from Qatar remain constrained.

sections.heading: US Crude Flows Cushion Prices as Permian Growth Moderates
sections.body:
Oil prices steadied in global trading as rising US crude inventories and steady supply offset renewed Gulf security risks following Iranian retaliatory strikes, Bloomberg and CBS News report. In the upstream US sector, OilPrice notes crude production growth in the Permian Basin has remained unexpectedly moderate despite war-driven price spikes above $100 a barrel, as producers prioritize capital discipline over rapid drilling.

In Iraq, Baghdad's closure of the Al-Sheeb border crossing with Iran has so far concentrated economic costs in Maysan Province, OilPrice writes, though a prolonged or wider border shutdown risks disrupting cross-border electricity, fuel, and trade flows vital to southern Iraq.
sections.whyItMatters: Moderate Permian output growth limits how quickly US shale can replace disrupted Middle Eastern barrels, leaving global oil balances reliant on strategic inventory buffers and Iraq-Iran border stability.

sections.heading: US Army Charts 75-Year Plan to Break China's Rare Earth Dominance
sections.body:
Federal efforts to build non-Chinese critical mineral supply chains are scaling into multi-decade industrial policy. OilPrice details how billions in Defense and Energy Department financing—including over $1 billion for MP Materials and a $1.6 billion government package for USA Rare Earth—tie into a long-term US Army and Pentagon push to eliminate reliance on Chinese rare-earth processing.

The push comes as major US defense primes face a 45-day Pentagon deadline to certify that heavy rare-earth magnets such as dysprosium and terbium are free of Chinese material, underscoring the gap between short-term compliance rules and the years needed to scale domestic refining.
sections.whyItMatters: Multi-billion-dollar federal financing for domestic mines and processors shows Washington treating rare-earth refining as permanent defense infrastructure rather than a temporary commodity bottleneck.

bottomLine: Clean baseload innovation and overland gas diplomacy are accelerating in parallel as traditional maritime and pipeline energy networks remain under siege. While Google bets on superhot geothermal and China deepens Central Asian gas ties, Europe faces heightened winter vulnerability as its largest pipeline gas supplier, Equinor, fends off a live cyberattack.
sources: OilPrice, The Hill, Bloomberg, CBS News
